name: Tomcat Manager Shell Upload
short_description: Upload a malicious WAR file to Tomcat Manager for remote code execution.
description: Apache Tomcat's Manager application allows deploying web apps. If you have valid credentials (often defaults like tomcat/tomcat), you can upload a malicious WAR file that gives you a shell. This is a common attack against misconfigured Java servers.

steps.title: Scan Tomcat
steps.explanation: Verify Tomcat is running on port 8080.

steps.title: Check for Manager interface
steps.explanation: The Manager app is at /manager/html. It requires authentication.

steps.title: Load the exploit
steps.explanation: This module creates a WAR file with a payload and uploads it via the Manager.

steps.title: Set the password
steps.explanation: Default password. In real scenarios, try common defaults or brute force.

steps.title: Choose a payload
steps.explanation: Use a Java reverse shell payload. This is more reliable than meterpreter for Tomcat.

steps.title: Set your listener IP
steps.explanation: This is the Kali attack box IP where the shell connects back.

steps.title: Execute the exploit
steps.explanation: Metasploit creates a WAR, uploads it, triggers execution, and catches the shell.

steps.title: Check your access (no prompt - just type!)
steps.explanation: IMPORTANT: There is NO prompt. The cursor is just blinking. Type 'id' and press Enter anyway - it works! Raw reverse shells don't show a prompt.

steps.title: Upgrade to a real prompt
steps.explanation: Raw reverse shells have no prompt. This spawns an interactive bash so you get a familiar prompt. (python3 pty.spawn works too if available)

steps.title: Explore the system
steps.explanation: List system users to understand the environment.

steps.title: Check the network
steps.explanation: See network interfaces. You're inside the Docker network now - potential pivot point.

steps.title: Look for other targets
steps.explanation: Docker often adds other container hostnames here. These are your next targets.

steps.title: One-command pwn (after you learn it)
steps.explanation: Exit the shell (type 'exit' twice) and try this. Now that you understand the attack, this script runs all the Metasploit steps automatically. Use it to demo or practice faster.

success_criteria: You have a root shell with a proper prompt and can explore the compromised system.
next_steps: Run 'env' to find secrets in environment variables
